2. Build the image as it stands and serve it, by hand: `docker build --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_BACKEND=local -t breathband-console:smoke .`, then `docker run --rm -d -p 8080:8080`, then curl `/`, `/cloud/login/` and `/cloud/login`. Record whether the build fails (for example the Next SWC binary on alpine or typecheck during `next build`) or a route doesn't return 200 HTML. Then remove the container.

3. Only if that run showed a real defect, make the smallest fix with no added comments (diff.no-new-comments). Likely candidates: `absolute_redirect off;` in nginx.conf so the 301 from /cloud/login to /cloud/login/ doesn't leak an internal host or port, or adding `.worktrees`, `.rivetari`, `coverage` and `*.log` to .dockerignore so the build context stays small. Keep `listen 8080` and `EXPOSE 8080`, and note each change and its reason for the PR body.

4. Create scripts/docker-smoke-lib.mjs, a pure ES module that uses node built-ins only. It exports: the smoke config (image tag, container name prefix, host port 8080, readiness timeout and interval); the route checks `[{ path: '/', expect: ['<h1 id="hero-h"', 'breathing.'] }, { path: '/cloud/login/', expect: ['<h1 id="login-h"', 'Sign in to BreathCloud'] }]`; and `checkResponse({ status, contentType, body }, route)`, which returns null or a clear error string covering status not 200, content-type not text/html, or missing expected text.

5. In the same module, export `waitUntilReady(url, { timeoutMs, intervalMs, fetchImpl })`. It polls with the global fetch and AbortSignal.timeout until a response arrives or the deadline passes, then throws an Error that names the URL and the last error it saw. Also export a `run(cmd, args)` helper around child_process.spawn (shell: false, inherit or capture stdio) that resolves to `{ code, stdout, stderr }` and turns ENOENT into 'docker CLI not found on PATH'.

6. Create scripts/docker-smoke.mjs as the entry point, with main steps in this order. (1) Run `docker info --format {{.ServerVersion}}`; if it exits non-zero, fail with 'Docker daemon isn't running (start Docker Desktop) …' plus its stderr. (2) Run `docker build --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_BACKEND=local -t breathband-console:smoke .` with cwd set to the repo root (resolved from import.meta.url) and stdio inherited. (3) Run `docker run -d --name breathband-smoke-<pid>-<time> -p 8080:8080 breathband-console:smoke` and keep the container name.

7. Continue main: wait until http://localhost:8080/ is ready, then fetch each route and apply checkResponse. Collect every failure and print a ✓ or ✗ line for each route. On failure also print `docker logs` for the container. Set process.exitCode to 0 only if every check passed, and always print an error message before a non-zero exit (build failure, port 8080 already in use from docker run's stderr, readiness timeout, check failures).

8. Guarantee cleanup: wrap everything after `docker run` in try/finally that runs `docker rm -f <name>` once the container name is known, even when docker run fails partway. Also register SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers that run the same idempotent cleanup and exit with code 130/143. If cleanup itself fails, report it with context rather than swallowing it.
9. Edit package.json and add `"docker:smoke": "node scripts/docker-smoke.mjs"`. Leave every existing script unchanged and add no dependency or devDependency (A3).

10. Add unit tests for the pure helpers in a new test file that `npm run test` actually picks up. vitest.config.mts only includes `src/**/*.test.ts` and must not be edited, so put a .test.ts file under src/, for example src/lib/dockerSmoke.test.ts importing '../../scripts/docker-smoke-lib.mjs'. If tsconfig or eslint reject that import, fall back to a node:test file at scripts/docker-smoke-lib.test.mjs plus a `test:scripts` npm script, and say so in the PR. Cover checkResponse (200 HTML with the text → null; 404, a non-HTML content-type and missing text → messages naming the path) and waitUntilReady (success after N failed fetches with a stub fetchImpl; timeout → Error naming the URL).

11. Run the new tests only: `npm run test -- related --run scripts/docker-smoke-lib.mjs <test file>` (or `node --test` for the fallback), then `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck`. Check that eslint (eslint-config-next covers .mjs) and tsc (allowJs: true) accept the new .mjs files with no suppressions, and fix any findings in the code.

12. Prove A1 end to end: run `npm run docker:smoke` with Docker running, confirm it builds, reaches readiness, prints ✓ for / and /cloud/login/, and exits 0. Then run `docker ps -a --filter name=breathband-smoke` and confirm it shows no container.

13. Prove the failure paths for A1/A2. (a) Temporarily point the route expectation at missing text through an env override, for example DOCKER_SMOKE_EXPECT_FAIL is not acceptable, so instead start a throwaway nginx on 8080 first and confirm the script fails clearly on 'port is already allocated' and leaves no smoke container. (b) Stop Docker Desktop and confirm a non-zero exit with the 'Docker daemon isn't running' message. (c) Press Ctrl-C during readiness and confirm the container is removed.

14. Make sure the infra-plan proof can be produced: the diff touches only scripts/**, package.json, a new test file, and Dockerfile/nginx.conf/.dockerignore only if step 3 needed it. It has no comments, no Markdown, nothing under gcloud/CI/firebase, and Dockerfile build args and port 8080 are unchanged. Then commit on chore/t-0009 with the attribution trailer.
